findings.what: Dragging (nothing) to player-base triggered an 'Auto Pay' path that attempted to send an exhaustRune move on the player's behalf (toast: 'Auto Pay failed: Move exhaustRune condition not met').
findings.why_wrong: DESIGN.md §Resource management: 'ready runes are NOT auto-counted or auto-exhausted. The player must explicitly tap runes first.' The UI should never auto-exhaust runes to pay a cost — the drag handler is violating stated design intent by even attempting it.
findings.reason: Screenshot /tmp/monkey-R1/03.png shows the toast "Auto Pay failed: Move 'exhaustRune' condition not met" after trace step 3 (drag " → player-base"), with a matching 400 console error. The drag handler at drag-drop.js:75-78 sets action="playCardAuto" when canAutoPay(cardId) is true, and on drop to player-base (drag-drop.js:306-310) calls autoPayAndPlay(cardId). auto-pay.js:129 schedules {moveId:"exhaustRune"} steps and auto-pay.js:197-199 sends them and surfaces the exact "Auto Pay failed: …" toast. This directly contradicts DESIGN.md:17 (§Resource management): "ready runes are NOT auto-counted or auto-exhausted. The player must explicitly tap runes first." The UI is auto-exhausting runes on the player's behalf, violating stated design intent.

findings.what: The empty-source drag still produced a server request (console 400) and surfaced 'Move exhaustRune condition not met' — yet the server's own legal-moves list in the same state includes exhaustRune for both Fury Rune and Chaos Rune (2 ready, runeExhausted=0).
findings.why_wrong: The error message directly contradicts observable game state: exhaustRune IS a legal move (rule 411 — a ready rune may be exhausted for energy). A player seeing '2/2 runes ready' plus 'cannot exhaust rune' will assume the game is broken. Root cause is the client sending a request with no valid card/rune id from an empty drag; it should validate the drag source client-side and send nothing, rather than surface a misleading server rejection.
findings.reason: Observable claim verified against exact sources. Step 3 drag (" → player-base") produced a console 400 (trace.json step[3].errs) and the UI toast "Auto Pay failed: Move 'exhaustRune' condition not met" is visible in /tmp/monkey-R1/03.png (toast rendered by auto-pay.js:199 `showToast(`Auto Pay failed: ${r.error}`)`; error string originates at packages/core/src/engine/rule-engine.ts:819). findings.what: After player-1 passed focus and the non-combat showdown at Back-Alley Bar closed (player-1 conquered, VP 0→1), the engine still offers `startShowdown` on that same battlefield. State shows `contested:true, contestedBy:player-1, controller:player-1, showdownComplete:false`, so the enumerator (`bf.contested && !bf.showdownComplete`) re-lists it and the UI shows a 'Start Showdown — Back-Alley Bar' button.

Once the sole occupant has conquered and controls the battlefield with no opposing units, no further showdown should be staged there — otherwise the player can loop empty showdowns forever. The passShowdownFocus/endShowdown path failed to set `showdownComplete=true` (or clear `contested`) on non-combat resolution the way rule 466.5.a does for combat.
findings.reason: Trace step 39 (post passShowdownFocus) shows battlefield player-2-bf-ogn-277-298 = {contested:true, contestedBy:"player-1", controller:"player-1", showdownComplete:false}, moves list includes startShowdown for that battlefield, and dom.actionButtons contains "Start Showdown Back-Alley Bar". The startShowdown enumerator at chain-moves.ts:1285 gates on `bf?.contested && !bf.showdownComplete`, so it re-lists the just-conquered battlefield. Rules 348.2/316.8.b/466.5.a confirm a closed non-combat showdown should not re-stage.

findings.what: On-play 'you may return a friendly unit at a battlefield to its owner's hand' resolves without prompting the player to choose a target or decline
findings.expected: RulesText says 'you MAY return A friendly unit' — player should be prompted to (a) opt in/out (optional trigger) and (b) select which of the 2 legal friendly units at the battlefield to return (Legion Rearguard or Grim Apothecary itself)
findings.observed: After passChainPriority the trigger auto-resolved with no pendingChoice/target prompt; engine auto-selected Legion Rearguard and bounced it to hand. Parser correctly emits optional:true, but the engine ignores it on resolution.
findings.reason: Parser emits optional:true on the ability (verified via parseAbilities on the rulesText → {type:"triggered", optional:true, effect:{type:"return-to-hand", target:{type:"unit",controller:"friendly",location:"battlefield"}}}). But when fireTriggers places the trigger on the chain (trigger-runner.ts:310-318) it stores only {cardId, controller, effect, triggered:true, type:"ability"} — the optional flag is dropped. executeResolvedItem (chain-moves.ts:156-249) never checks for an opt-in and executes the effect unconditionally; effect-executor.ts:1241-1248 likewise auto-applies case "optional" with the comment "auto-apply for now". No pendingChoice yes/no prompt exists anywhere for optional triggered abilities. The auto-selection of Legion Rearguard follows from target-resolver.ts:150-152, which unconditionally excludes sourceCardId — leaving exactly one option, so chain-moves.ts:221 (options.length >= 2) does not fire the choose-target prompt and the sole remaining target is bounced.

findings.what: 'When I become ready' trigger does not fire during Awaken phase readying

findings.observed: Unit readied (exhausted:false) but Might stayed at 5, meta.buffed=false, no log entry for the trigger, no chain item; state confirmed via API zones dump
findings.reason: ven-071-166's trigger cannot fire because the card definition ships with `"abilities": []` and `"parseSuccess": false` (ven.json:2216-2217). The engine's registry reads abilities straight from that JSON (card-lookup.ts:164-166 → trigger-runner.ts:71-96 `toTriggerableAbilities`), so `findMatchingTriggers` sees zero triggerable abilities for this card and nothing is placed on the chain — Might stays at base 5. The Awaken flow itself DOES emit a ready event (riftbound-flow.ts:224-227) and the matcher supports `ready` (trigger-matcher.ts:87), so the report's "Layer: engine" is off: root cause is the card data/parser, not the awaken/trigger machinery. Secondary latent mismatch: the parser pattern emits `event: "become-ready"` (parser/index.ts:3982) while the engine fires `type: "ready"` and EVENT_MAP has no `become-ready` entry (trigger-matcher.ts:66-92, 160-164), so even a successful parse would still fail to match until the event names are aligned.

findings.what: On-play kill trigger drops the '3 [Might] or less' constraint
findings.expected: rulesText: 'kill an enemy unit with 3 [Might] or less' — the target filter should restrict to enemy units whose Might is ≤3
findings.observed: Runtime chain effect after playing was {"type":"kill","target":{"type":"unit","controller":"enemy"}} — no might filter present. parseKillEffect (parser/index.ts ~L700) matches the 'with N [Might] or less' clause via a non-capturing group (?:\s+with\s+.+)? and passes only richMatch[1] ('an enemy unit') to parseCardTarget, so the Might≤3 restriction is silently discarded and any enemy unit is a legal target.
findings.reason: Card sfd-158-221 (sandshifter.ts:13) has rulesText "When you play me, kill an enemy unit with 3 [Might] or less." Runtime parseAbilities output is {"type":"kill","target":{"type":"unit","controller":"enemy"}} — no Might≤3 filter. Root cause: parser/index.ts:700 regex captures the target as group 1 ending at "unit", while the trailing clause is swallowed by the non-capturing `(?:\s+with\s+.+)?`; line 703/728 pass only richMatch[1] ("an enemy unit") to parseCardTarget, which (lines 399-467) has no Might-constraint handling. The "with 3 [Might] or less" restriction is silently discarded, making any enemy unit a legal kill target. Verified by executing the parser via bun.

findings.what: "When I attack" trigger never fires
findings.expected: Per rule 464.2.c.3/464.2.e, when combat opens Azir gains the Attacker designation and his "When I attack, you may move any number of your token units to this battlefield" trigger goes on the chain, prompting the player to choose token units to move.
findings.observed: Moved Azir into battlefield player-2-bf-ogn-275-298 alongside an enemy Recruit token — a combat showdown opened (interaction.showdown.isCombatShowdown=true, attackingPlayer=player-1) but combatRole stayed null on every unit, chain=null, pendingChoice=null. No attack event is emitted anywhere in the engine (only trigger-matcher/game-events/dispatcher declare the type; movement.ts startShowdownState and combat.ts assignAttacker never call fireTriggers with type:"attack"). The Sand Soldier token at the other battlefield stayed put.
findings.reason: The "attack" GameEvent is declared (game-events.ts:14), mapped (trigger-matcher.ts:67), and registered (dispatcher.ts:92), and cards like sfd-177-221 get a `trigger: { event: "attack", on: "self" }` via parser/index.ts:3690 — but no non-test engine code ever calls `fireTriggers` with `type: "attack"`. The combat-open path at movement.ts:389 calls `startShowdownState(...)` (setting attackingPlayer on the showdown) without assigning combatRole to any unit and without firing attack/defend events; the alternate open path chain-moves.ts:1307 does the same. combat.ts:145-158 `assignAttacker` sets `combatRole: "attacker"` but likewise never fires an attack event. Consequently Azir's "When I attack" trigger can never reach the chain. The rules-audit test comment at combat.test.ts:1006-1011 describes the intended `fireTriggers({type: "attack" | "defend"})` behavior but the test only manually pre-populates the chain — the emission is unimplemented.

findings.what: Parser drops the "token" filter and treats "any number" as "all"
findings.expected: parseAbilities should yield a triggered ability whose move effect targets a player-chosen subset of friendly *token* units (something like target:{type:"unit",controller:"friendly",isToken:true,quantity:"anyNumber"}).
findings.observed: parseAbilities("...move any number of your token units to this battlefield") returned effect:{type:"move",to:"here",target:{quantity:"all",type:"unit",controller:"friendly"}}. Even if the attack event fired, this would forcibly move every friendly unit (token or not) instead of letting the player choose which token units to move.
findings.reason: Verified by running parseAbilities on Azir's rules text — output is exactly {target:{quantity:"all",type:"unit",controller:"friendly"},to:"here",type:"move"}. At index.ts:1067-1083 the "any number of" move regex captures the qualifier word ("token") in group 2 `((?:\w+\s+)?units?)` but never reads anyNumberMatch[2], so the token filter is silently dropped; and line 1072-1073 hardcodes quantity:"all" instead of an anyNumber/player-choice quantity. Result: the effect would forcibly move every friendly unit (token or non-token) rather than letting the player choose a subset of token units.

findings.reason: Parser at index.ts:3265-3279 emits the [Empower] keyword as `{cost, effect:{target:"self",type:"empower"}, type:"activated"}` with no "not-empowered" restriction/condition. The engine's activateAbility condition (chain-moves.ts:622-821) and enumerator (chain-moves.ts:822+) contain zero references to `empower`/`empowered` — they check zone, ownership, while-level, timing, and cost affordability (energy/power/xp/exhaust/discard/kill), but never `meta.empowered`. No `notEmpowered`/`not-empowered`/`onlyIfNot` token exists anywhere in riftbound-engine or riftbound-cards. So once meta.empowered=true, activateAbility for the Empower ability remains offered and payable, violating rule 827.1.c.1 ("Play only if not Empowered").

findings.what: 'When I move' trigger auto-deals damage without a 'you may' / target-selection prompt
findings.expected: rulesText 'you may deal 1 to a unit at a battlefield I moved to or from' — controller should be prompted to opt in and choose which unit (2 valid units were present at destination)
findings.observed: Trigger went on chain; after a single passChainPriority it resolved and dealt 1 damage to the first unit at the destination automatically. No pendingChoice / chooseTarget move was ever offered.
findings.reason: The "you may" opt-in is dropped by the engine. Parser output for ven-021-166 (verified via runtime parse) is `{type:"triggered", trigger:{event:"move",on:"self"}, effect:{type:"damage",amount:1,target:{type:"unit",location:"battlefield"}}, optional:true}` (parser/index.ts:4104-4108, 4274-4276). When the move fires, trigger-runner.ts:306-321 places only `{cardId, controller, effect, triggered, type}` on the chain — `optional` is discarded. `executeResolvedItem` (chain-moves.ts:156-249) never checks any optional flag, and `resolvePendingChoice` for choose-target (pending-choice.ts:91-126) enumerates only target picks with no skip/decline option. A repo-wide grep confirms `optional` is copied at trigger-runner.ts:84 and never read anywhere else in the engine. So the controller cannot decline the "you may" trigger — the effect always resolves. Repro (Akali at base + 2 enemy units at bf-2, standardMove → pass P1 → pass P2) shows the chain item has no `optional` field. NOTE: the report's secondary claim that no choose-target prompt appears is inaccurate — the same repro shows `pendingChoice:{type:"choose-target",options:["enemy-a","enemy-b"]}` is set at chain-moves.ts:221-230 when ≥2 legal units exist; only the "you may" opt-in is missing.

findings.what: Move-trigger target filter does not restrict to 'battlefield I moved to or from'
findings.expected: Effect target should be scoped to units at the source or destination battlefield of the move
findings.observed: Chain item effect was {type:'damage',amount:1,target:{type:'unit',location:'battlefield'}} — generic 'any unit at any battlefield' with no from/to zone constraint.
findings.reason: ven-021-166 (Akali, Deadly Weapon) has no hand-coded ability (ven.json:920 abilities:[null]; no ven/ dir under cards/), so it relies on the rules-text parser. Running parseAbilities on the card's rulesText yields the triggered effect {type:'damage',amount:1,target:{type:'unit',location:'battlefield'}} — exactly the observed chain item. Root cause: parseCardTarget at parser/index.ts:442-447 does a plain substring check `lower.includes("at a battlefield")` and sets location:'battlefield', silently discarding the trailing "I moved to or from" qualifier; there is no location value or filter representing the move's source/destination zones. The engine's target-resolver.ts:136-140 then treats location 'battlefield' as any zone starting with "battlefield", so every unit on every battlefield is a legal target instead of only units at the from/to battlefield of the triggering move.

findings.what: UI shows no Empowered indicator and Might stays at base value after Empower
findings.expected: After Empower resolves, card should visually indicate Empowered and display effective Might 4 (base 3 + staticMightBonus 1)
findings.observed: Card DOM class remained 'card type-unit exhausted card--exhausted card--summoning-sick' (no empowered class, no might badge); snapshot.might=3 (server sends def.might, not effective).
findings.reason: renderCardElement (renderer.js:616-678) builds the class list with checks for meta.exhausted/stunned/buffed (lines 618-623) but has no `card.meta?.empowered` check, so no empowered class is ever added — grep for "empower" across apps/riftbound-app/public/ returns zero hits. The card template (lines 659-678) renders only a damage badge (line 675) and never renders might, so no effective-might badge exists. Separately, server.ts:687 populates snapshot `might` from `def.might` (base 3) rather than base + meta.mightModifier + meta.staticMightBonus, so even the value sent is 3, not 4. Card ven-021-166 (ven.json:900-918) has base might 3 and `[Empowered]> I have +1 [Might]`, so after Empower resolves the engine sets meta.empowered=true (effect-executor.ts:944) and static-abilities.ts:349-353 sets staticMightBonus=1 → effective 4, but the UI has no code path to surface either.

findings.what: '[Exhaust]: Play two Bird tokens' ability is activatable while the unit is at base
findings.expected: rulesText 'Use this ability only while I'm at a battlefield' — activateAbility should not be offered when Poro is in the base zone
findings.observed: With Poro ready at base, availableMoves included activateAbility{abilityIndex:0,cardId:poro}. Location restriction is not enforced by move enumeration.
findings.reason: The activateAbility move's condition (chain-moves.ts:623-821) and enumerator (chain-moves.ts:822-1054) never read ability.restrictions. The zone gate at :640-648 explicitly accepts zone === "base", and no subsequent code checks the "self-at-battlefield" restriction that the parser attaches (riftbound-cards/src/parser/index.ts:3531-3537). collectActivatedAbilities (:317-347) also does no restriction filtering. The only engine consumer of "self-at-battlefield" is abilities/trigger-matcher.ts:137, which handles triggered-ability restrictions, not activated ones. So a ready Ultrasoft Poro (unl-160-219) in base passes every check and is enumerated as activateAbility{abilityIndex:0}, violating "Use this ability only while I'm at a battlefield".

findings.what: Created Bird tokens surface to client as type 'unknown' with raw-ID name and no might
findings.expected: Snapshot/UI should show tokens as unit cards named 'Bird' with might=1 and Deflect keyword
findings.observed: Snapshot: {name:'token-bird-1785961560833-0', type:'unknown', might:undefined, defId:'token-def-bird'}; DOM class 'card type-unknown', card-name shows the instance ID. effect-executor.ts:1142 registers the token def under the instance-ID key, but server.ts buildGameSnapshot looks it up by cardInstance.definitionId ('token-def-bird') → miss.
findings.reason: Key mismatch verified. effect-executor.ts:1129 builds tokenId="token-{name}-{Date.now()}-{i}" and :1141 calls registry.register(tokenId, {...}) — the def is stored under the INSTANCE id. Meanwhile ctx.createCardInZone (chain-moves.ts:96-111) derives slug from that same tokenId and stamps the card instance with definitionId="token-def-{slug}" (:107). server.ts buildGameSnapshot :668-669 does registry.get(cardInstance.definitionId) ?? getGlobalCardRegistry().get(cardInstance.definitionId), i.e. looks up "token-def-bird". The static set registry (server.ts:114 getCardRegistry()) has no such entry, and the global registry only has it under the instance id, so def=undefined. Snapshot then emits cardType "unknown" (:680), name=cardId (:688), might undefined (:687), definitionId="token-def-bird" (:682) — exactly the observed payload. The only path that DOES register "token-def-{slug}" is the manual addToken move (token.ts:131-140), which ability-driven create-token (unl-160-219 Ultrasoft Poro) does not go through.

findings.what: [Flow] [2] keyword not offered — cannot play Dredge Up from trash
findings.expected: After resolving from hand, card sits in trash and a playSpell (or flow-specific) move should be available to replay it from trash for [2], banishing it afterward
findings.observed: Card is in trash (trash count=1), player has 4 energy, but move enumeration lists no move referencing player-1-main-999-ven-049-166; no ven/ set directory exists under packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/ and no Flow keyword handling found in riftbound-engine
findings.reason: ven-049-166 "Dredge Up" is defined only in data/sets/ven.json:1632 (no ven/ dir under cards/src/cards/ — only ogn/ogs/sfd/unl exist). Its rulesText carries "[Flow] [2]" but: (1) the parser's keyword lists at riftbound-cards/src/parser/index.ts:4364-4398 and parsers/keyword-parser.ts:25 (COST_KEYWORDS = ["Accelerate","Equip","Repeat"]) do not include "Flow", so no flow cost is ever parsed onto the card; (2) the engine's playSpell move gates on zone === "hand" — condition at cards.ts:1053 `if (zone !== "hand") return false;` and enumerator at cards.ts:1156-1162 iterates only `getCardsInZone("hand", ...)`. No other move in game-definition/moves/ enumerates spells from the "trash" zone (grep for trash shows only discard/recycle/kill destinations, never a play source). Grep for the literal string "Flow" as a keyword in riftbound-engine/src and riftbound-cards/src/parser returns zero hits. Therefore with the card in trash and 4 energy, move enumeration correctly (per current code) offers nothing referencing the card — the Flow keyword is unimplemented at both the parser layer and the engine move layer.

findings.what: No Reflection token is created
findings.expected: On resolve, a ready Reflection (unl-t06) unit token appears at player-1's base as a copy of the chosen unit (Legion Rearguard, might 2)
findings.observed: After chain resolves, base still contains only the original Legion Rearguard (1 unit); no token in base or any bfZone. Chain item's effect was solely {type:'grant-keyword', keyword:'Temporary'} — no create-token / copy effect present
findings.reason: mirror-image.ts:4-16 declares no `abilities` array, so enrich-cards.ts:29 falls back to parseAbilities on the rulesText. The parser's unit-token regex (parser/index.ts:2010-2026) requires a `:rb_might:` value and rejects "Play a ready Reflection unit token to your base" (no might), so only the "Give it [Temporary]" sentence is parsed. Verified by running parseAbilities on the rulesText — output is exactly [{type:'spell', effect:{type:'grant-keyword', keyword:'Temporary', target:{type:'unit'}}}], matching the observed chain item. No create-token / copy effect exists at runtime, so no Reflection token is ever created. Contrast keeper-of-masks.ts:13-31, which hand-authors a `create-token` ability for the same Reflection token.

findings.what: [Temporary] is granted to the chosen source unit instead of the (non-existent) token
findings.expected: The newly-created Reflection token receives [Temporary]; the chosen original unit is unaffected
findings.observed: Chain item targets=['player-1-main-5-ogn-010-298'] (the original Legion Rearguard) with grant-keyword Temporary — the original unit gets Temporary and will be killed at its controller's next Beginning Phase
findings.reason: mirror-image.ts:4-16 defines only rulesText with no explicit abilities; parseAbilities() on that text yields a single effect {type:"grant-keyword", keyword:"Temporary", target:{type:"unit"}} — no create-token, no become-copy. At play time the "Choose a unit" target is bound on the chain item (cards.ts:1081 → chain-moves.ts:197,238 sets ctx.boundTargets). On resolution effect-executor.ts:991 calls getTargetIds, which at effect-executor.ts:121-122 unconditionally returns ctx.boundTargets when present, so Temporary is granted to the chosen original unit (e.g. player-1-main-5-ogn-010-298). No Reflection token is ever created (create-token case at effect-executor.ts:1106 is never reached), and even if it were, tokenId is never written back into ctx for later "it" references.

findings.what: No 'choose a battlefield where you have units' prompt when playing the spell
findings.expected: Per rulesText, player is prompted to choose a battlefield they have units at (only Abandoned Hall qualified in test); the chain item should carry that choice.
findings.observed: playSpell went straight onto the chain with no targets/choices bound and no pendingChoice; the enriched card ability has no choose-battlefield step at all (sequence is [move→base, modify-might]).
findings.reason: Moonfall (unl-198-219) at moonfall.ts:4-16 declares no `abilities`, so enrichCard() (enrich-cards.ts:22-38) calls parseAbilities() on the rulesText. Running the parser on the actual rulesText yields exactly `{type:"spell", effect:{type:"sequence", effects:[{type:"move", target:{type:"unit",controller:"enemy",quantity:{upTo:1}}, to:"base"}, {type:"modify-might", amount:-2, target:{type:"unit",controller:"enemy"}, duration:"turn"}]}}` — no choose-battlefield descriptor at all. The "Choose a battlefield where you have units." sentence is dropped (the strip-preamble regex at parser/index.ts:3628 only matches unit/gear/spell, not battlefield), and "to that battlefield" falls through parseLocationString's default at parser/patterns/effects.ts:584 to `"base"`. In playSpell (game-definition/moves/cards.ts:1043-1300), the enumerator only binds caster-chosen targets when `spellEffect.target` is a card-type descriptor (a sequence has none, and battlefield-type is explicitly excluded), so it emits `{playerId, cardId}` with no targets; the reducer then calls addToChain at cards.ts:1279-1283 with `{cardId, controller, effect, targets:undefined, type:"spell"}` and sets no pendingChoice. Matches the observed behavior: spell goes straight onto the chain with no battlefield choice bound.

findings.expected: Abandoned Hall's trigger fires AFTER the spell fully resolves (rule 419.4.a / 350.1 / 383.2.c). A unit moved INTO Abandoned Hall by that spell is present when the trigger's target is chosen and CAN be picked for +1 Might; a unit moved AWAY is no longer 'here' and CANNOT be picked.
findings.observed: Abandoned Hall's triggered ability never fires at all in the live engine. With P1's Legion Rearguard sitting at Abandoned Hall (battlefield-player-1-bf-unl-205-219), P1 played two spells (Meditation ogn-048-298, Mobilize ogn-134-298); each went on the chain and resolved, but no Abandoned Hall trigger was ever added — interaction.nextChainItemId did not increment past the spell's own chain item and the unit's Might stayed at 2. Consequently a unit moved INTO Abandoned Hall by a spell cannot be chosen (no prompt is ever offered), contradicting the ruling's 'yes' half. The direct moved-into scenario via Thrill of the Hunt (unl-184-219) also failed to complete because resolvePendingChoice for choose-destination rejects battlefield picks with 'Target zone player-1-bf-unl-205-219 does not exist'.
findings.notes: Root cause of the divergence is registry setup, not the timing rule. Battlefield card instances are created via server.ts:722 registerCard(), which writes internal.cards/cardMetas but never calls getGlobalCardRegistry().register(), so card-lookup.ts getAbilities('player-1-bf-unl-205-219') returns [] and trigger-runner.ts toTriggerableAbilities() yields nothing for battlefieldRow cards. The engine's timing implementation (chain-moves.ts:252-286) is otherwise correct — it fires play-spell only at resolution and reorders effect-added pending plays above the queued triggers (Abandoned Hall named in the comment) — so once the registry gap is fixed the ruling should MATCH. Secondary bug: effect-executor.ts:782 builds choose-destination options from Object.keys(draft.battlefields) (no 'battlefield-' prefix) but pending-choice.ts:193 passes the picked value straight to zones.moveCard, which needs the prefixed zone id. Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-a8681f703fd3fa17.png. Game id 89da4256-c7ea-4302-891a-04750077ddd6.

findings.expected: Per the ruling: when a spell like Thrill of the Hunt resolves, the replayed unit is appended to the chain as a pending item, then Abandoned Hall's 'when a player plays a spell' trigger is appended after it. Pending items finalize in append order (337.1.b) and units resolve immediately on finalization (337.2), so the replayed unit lands at Abandoned Hall BEFORE the trigger's target is chosen, making the replayed unit a valid choice for the +1 Might buff.
findings.observed: After Thrill of the Hunt (unl-184-219) resolved on Determined Sentry (unl-111-219), the chain contained ONLY the pending replay item (chain-2). Abandoned Hall's play-spell trigger was never added to the chain — interaction.nextChainItemId advanced 1→3 (Thrill=chain-1, replay=chain-2) with no chain-3 for the trigger. A follow-up plain spell (Mobilize) also produced no Abandoned Hall trigger (nextChainItemId 3→4 only). Because the trigger never fires, there is no target-choice prompt at all, so the replayed unit cannot be chosen. Separately, the replay's choose-destination step is broken for battlefields: picking 'player-1-bf-unl-205-219' (the option the engine offers) fails server-side with 'Target zone player-1-bf-unl-205-219 does not exist' — pending-choice.ts:193-196 passes the bare battlefield id to zones.moveCard, which requires the 'battlefield-' prefixed zone key. Only 'base' works, so the unit cannot even be placed at Abandoned Hall via the replay.
findings.notes: Two distinct engine bugs surfaced: (1) Abandoned Hall's play-spell trigger does not fire in practice — chain-moves.ts:255-285 calls fireTriggers({type:'play-spell'}) and even has explicit reordering logic commented for this exact Thrill-of-the-Hunt/Abandoned-Hall scenario, but no matched trigger is queued (likely a registry/matcher gap for battlefieldRow instance ids). (2) effect-executor.ts:782 populates choose-destination options from Object.keys(draft.battlefields) (bare bf ids), while pending-choice.ts:195 hands that id straight to zones.moveCard without the 'battlefield-' prefix, throwing at operations-impl.ts:207. findings.expected: Per the ruling: when Alpha Strike is finalized on the chain, the caster (1) chooses a friendly unit as an explicit standard target, then (2) chooses up to N enemy units at battlefields as split targets (N = that friendly unit's current might), may choose fewer including zero, and (3) all of those choices are locked in on the chain item at finalization before opponents can respond.
findings.observed: Setup (game 9f60b213): friendly Legion Rearguard (might 2) in base, 4 enemy Recruit tokens at two battlefields, Alpha Strike in hand. The playSpell enumeration offered exactly one Alpha Strike option: {targets:["player-1-main-11-ogn-010-298"]} — only the friendly reference unit. After executing playSpell, the chain item stored targets:[friendly-id] and NO pendingChoice was raised for enemy split-target selection. The caster was never asked which enemy units to target, how many, or given the option to choose zero. After both players passed, the spell resolved with no split-target prompt at resolution either (in this run 0 damage was dealt because the enemy token instances are not registered in the global card registry, so resolveTarget's cardType filter excluded them — a separate addToken bug). Code confirms the divergence independent of the token issue: cards.ts:1206-1225 (playSpell enumerator) only enumerates the amount.might friendly-reference target and never enumerates enemy split targets; chain-moves.ts:197 passes only that single-element targets array as boundTargets; effect-executor.ts:544-548 then falls into the `else` branch and auto-selects `legalPool.slice(0, n)` at RESOLUTION — the caster cannot pick which enemy units, cannot pick fewer than N, and the choice is not locked at finalization.
findings.notes: Partial match: the friendly reference unit IS bound as an explicit target at finalization (matches ruling). Divergence: enemy split targets are neither caster-chosen nor bound at finalization — the engine auto-assigns the first N legal enemy units at resolution time, contradicting rules 355.14.b/c and 355.15 as cited in the ruling. Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-6b3effc73787ce91.png. Relevant files: /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/alpha-strike.ts, /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts (lines 1200-1231), /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts (lines 454-589).

findings.expected: Per 355.14.h/.h.1: with 3 enemy targets chosen at finalization and the friendly reference unit's Might reduced from 3 to 2 before resolution, the controller is prompted to choose exactly 1 target to drop (of their choice); the remaining 2 targets each receive at least 1 damage; the controller may NOT drop 2 targets to concentrate both damage on one.
findings.observed: Set up Safety Inspector (3M, p1 base) + 3 enemy 1M units (Mutated Mouser, Sharkling, Sinister Poro) at p2's battlefield. Played Alpha Strike (targets=[inspector]), applied modifyBuff deltaMight=-1 while on chain (effective might 3→2), then both players passed. Result: Mouser and Sharkling took 1 damage each and died; Poro took 0; NO pendingChoice was raised. Engine auto-selected legalPool.slice(0,2) at resolution — the controller was never asked which target to drop.
findings.notes: Damage total DID shrink correctly (2, not 3) and exactly 1 target was effectively dropped, so the 'cannot drop extra to concentrate' outcome holds vacuously. But 355.14.h says 'the player determines which Targets cease being Targets' and the ruling says 'drop 2 targets of your choice' — the engine gives no such choice. Root cause: split targets are never bound at play time (playSpell only binds the amount:{might:...} reference unit; the enemy target descriptor has quantity:'all'), so effect-executor.ts:517 sees boundTargets.length==1 and falls through to the else branch (legalPool.slice(0,n)) instead of the 355.14.h drop-prompt branch at :527-543 — that branch is dead code for Alpha Strike as currently modeled. Separately, addToken tokens don't work with Alpha Strike at all (registry keyed by definitionId 'token-def-*' but getEffectiveMight/resolveTarget look up by instance id → 0 damage); had to use tutor+duplicateCard for real card instances. Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-013355072ffd6542.png

findings.expected: Per the ruling: Yes — after Arcane Shift banishes your only unit at a controlled battlefield, the replayed unit sits on the chain as a pending item, the turn stays closed so cleanup step 4 (rule 323.6) does not strip battlefield control, and when the pending unit is finalized you can choose to play it back to that same battlefield.
findings.observed: Setup: player-1 controls battlefield player-1-bf-unl-205-219 with a single friendly unit (dup-player-1-main-2-ogn-010-298-1); enemy unit at bf-2 for the damage clause. Played Arcane Shift → resolved chain: friendly unit banished, pending replay item (chain-2, effect {type:move,to:choose}) added to chain, damage killed enemy, spell self-banished. While chain-2 was on the chain, bf-1.controller correctly stayed player-1 (cleanup gated on open state — matches ruling). Resolved chain-2 → pendingChoice {type:choose-destination, options:["base","player-1-bf-unl-205-219","player-2-bf-ogn-275-298"]}. The same battlefield IS offered as an option. HOWEVER, executing resolvePendingChoice with pickedZoneId="player-1-bf-unl-205-219" fails: {success:false, error:"Target zone player-1-bf-unl-205-219 does not exist"}. Picking "base" succeeds. Net effect: the engine offers the same battlefield but selecting it errors, so the player cannot actually replay there.
findings.notes: Rule logic (chain keeps state closed → control not stripped → same bf offered) is correctly implemented — see effect-executor.ts:1337-1362 (case 'play', comment cites 354.2/354.3/309.1/323.6/355.2) and cleanup/state-based-checks.ts:296-319 (isOpenState gate). The DIVERGENCE is a zone-id bug: effect-executor.ts:782 builds options as ['base', ...Object.keys(draft.battlefields)] (bare bf ids like 'player-1-bf-unl-205-219'), and pending-choice.ts:188-196 passes the picked option straight to zones.moveCard as targetZoneId, but the actual zone id is 'battlefield-player-1-bf-unl-205-219'. The failed move also removes the card from banishment before throwing, leaving it in no zone (state corruption). Secondary observation: options include the uncontrolled bf-2 as well, which is over-permissive vs rule 355.2.a (and would let attackers replay to an attacking battlefield contrary to the ruling's second paragraph), but that is masked by the same zone-id bug. Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-ee735b43996dcbd3.png.
